chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about young children who have wealth in the possession of their father or their brother, whether zakat is obligatory upon their wealth. He said: 'Zakat is not obligatory upon their wealth until it is put to use (invested/grown). When it is put to use, zakat becomes obligatory. As for that which is held in reserve (not yet invested), there is no zakat upon it.'
ai.seo_question: When does zakat become obligatory on a child's wealth held by a guardian?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the principle of 'nushu' (growth) in zakat for minors, distinguishing between passive wealth held by guardians and active capital that generates profit. It reflects the Shia juristic view that zakat is tied to the productive state of the asset rather than mere possession, a nuance critical in the calculation of khums and zakat for children's inheritances.
